newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague sets tone for gloomy E.Europe bourses.
newsitem.headline: Prague sets tone for gloomy E.Europe bourses.

text.p: Central and east European stock markets continued in bearish mood this week with Budapest the region's only gainer and Prague taking the brunt of faltering confidence by foreign investors, analysts said.

Losses to blue-chip stocks, which were especially heavy in the Czech Republic, pushed the Central European Share Index (CESI) down 0.9 percent to 1,396.96. Most of the region's bourses were closed on Friday for All Saints Day.
BUDAPEST
A seven session decline in Hungarian share prices came to an end on Wednesday and modest gains in the following two days pushed the BUX index up 68 points from the start of the week to 3,614.2.
Traders were mostly optimistic that companies' January-September earnings reports, to be submitted to the bourse by November 15, would boost the market.
PRAGUE
Czech shares had another dismal week despite a small rebound on Friday from some major issues. The PX50 fell 3.3 percent during the week to end on Friday at 504.1.
The sharpest fallers among major issues were Komercni Banka and SPT Telecom.

But on Friday, Komercni spearheaded a light rebound from heavily capitalised issues after publishing nine month profit figures which were within the range of analysts expectations. However, dealers did not expect any sustained uptrend to emerge in the near future.

Major issues have been hit by a general decline in confidence in the Czech equities market, which is widely criticised for its lack of transparency and inadequate protection for minority shareholders.
WARSAW

On Wednesday and Thursday, the WIG rose 4.9-percent, leaving the main market flat for the week at 13,497.9 points. But analysts saw little chance of a strong early rebound by the index, which has lost 14.6 percent since October 9.

The main market's biggest loser this week, construction firm Espebepe, was down 18.8 percent. Analysts said the decline was probably caused by a statement from the company's president last week that it might go bankrupt.
BUCHAREST
The Bucharest bourse, which saw a rebound on Tuesday, slipped on Thursday, with turnover sagging to 39 million lei.
With investors in a wait-and-see mood ahead of Sunday's general elections, most shares drifted lower, sending two independent indices to year lows.
The VAB and the BIG fell 1.9 percent from the previous session to 285.3 and 284.29 points, respectively.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) was in gloomy mood with the SAX index falling through the 200 point level and dealers seeing little hope of a rebound in the near future.
Traders said the mood on the market was partly a knock on-effect from neighbouring bourses.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks ended a shortened trading week mixed on Thursday ahead of a public holiday.

Market watchers predicted most prices would continue to dip next week, although at a slower pace, with investors seen likely to hold back until the government resolves some disputed share ownership issues.
BULGARIA

No corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market for the third week in a row after the Bulgarian Securities and Stock Exchange Commission (SSEC) suspended trading until companies meet new legal requirements.

Under Bulgaria's stock trading law, public companies had until September 19 to submit to the SSEC a detailed report on the size and distribution of their capital and a list of their shareholders. None of them has yet fulfilled their new obligations, the BSE said.
TIRANA
Tirana's Stock Exchange saw four transactions of 364-day treasury bills on Monday and Thursday but no state bonds changed hands, an exchange official said.
LJUBLJANA
In Ljubljana, share prices eased 0.1 percent to 1,192.07. Total turnover was 1.2 billion tolars ($8.7 million).
Financial consultancy Dadas was the sharpest decliner, falling 24.3 percent, while Primofin was the biggest gainer with a 66.8 percent rise.
CESI

The Central European Share Index (CESI) was modified effective October 31 to include Slovenian and Slovak stocks in addition to Hungarian, Czech and Polish. The expanded index basket now contains 73 shares against 50 previously.
